audit.whatIsWrong: tldr and winCon described a 'poke war' where you 'survive the poke tax'. Kassadin has no poke and no waveclear before his ultimate — the lane's shape is the exact opposite.
audit.why: Riot's text gives him a 650-range Q that shields him, a single-target W auto-empower and an E that must charge off nearby spellcasts. His pressure arrives at 6 with Riftwalk, not before.
audit.corrected: tldr, winCon, report[0].t, report[1].t and enemyWin rewritten around 'free before 6, leashed only by grounding after'.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gave Locke levels 6 and first item and called two-plus items Skill, while the whys on the same rows said 'Level 6 is even', 'First item stays even' and 'hand Kass the lane'. Two layers, two answers, and neither matched the packet chart.
audit.why: Packet levelChart reads Skill through the first six rows and Kassadin at two-plus items. Riftwalk drops from 5s to 2s by rank 3 and stacks damage, which is the real late-game shift.
audit.corrected: Rows 4, 5 and 6 flipped as matched full/content pairs (Locke->Skill, Locke->Skill, Skill->Kassadin), ratings adjusted, and all three whys rewritten to say why.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction of the matchup was never stated: Locke's R applies grounding and Riftwalk is a dash, so inside the zone Kassadin cannot blink. Separately, wants.foe[1] claimed Null Sphere's shield absorbs your W burst.
audit.why: Locke R flags list grounding ('shuts off enemy dashes'); Kassadin R is flagged as a dash. Null Sphere's own description says the shield 'absorbs magic damage' — Locke's W is flagged trueDamage, which is not magic, and Void Stone reduces magic damage but not true damage.
audit.corrected: Grounding written into phases[4], phases[6], spikes[1], spikes[3], report[5].t and dosFull[0].d; wants.foe[1] corrected to name his shield's real target (your on-hit magic damage, not your W).

audit.why: Riftwalk's 5s base cooldown is short enough that 'wait for it to be down' is not real advice — the punishable window is his mana, not his timer, and the text no longer promises a Riftwalk-down commit after the rewrite.
audit.corrected: Commit language re-keyed to the grounding zone rather than to his ult cooldown.

edits.before: Purgatory online: top lane's long brawls now end at YOUR floor. Anyone who all-ins you under a third is volunteering for the totem.
edits.after: Purgatory grounds, and grounding denies Riftwalk — but his ult is up every 5s, so he blinks first. Even at 6 unless you catch him.

edits.before: Lich Bane spike — the blink-consume chunk finally out-numbers their sustain. Cash kill windows before their second item re-rigs the math.
edits.after: Lich Bane pays, but Void Stone cuts magic damage and Null Sphere shields more of it — your W's true damage is the part that still lands.

edits.before: You out-execute but they out-stat: split where the totem punishes 1v1 greed, and never brawl at full HP — your kit votes at the bottom of the bar.
edits.after: His game now: Riftwalk falls to 2s and stacks damage, so he leaves every Purgatory zone. Fight only where a teammate's CC holds him in it.

edits.before: R Riftwalk arrives and the lane flips: Kass can now blink onto you or escape your E Ashen Pursuit dash entirely. Your R Purgatory execute still threatens him, so 6-vs-6 is roughly even, but he stops being free.
edits.after: R Riftwalk (5s at rank 1) arrives and the lane flips: Kass can blink onto you or out of your E entirely. Your R grounds — inside the zone Riftwalk is switched off, so spend it to trap the blink, not to open the fight.

edits.before: This is Kassadin's game — stacked Riftwalks let him blink-kill you or dodge your entire combo, and his magic shield eats your AP burst. If you didn't build a lead by 9, he out-scales and out-mobilities you hard.
edits.after: This is Kassadin's game — a 2s Riftwalk lets him blink-kill you or dodge your combo, and Void Stone's magic reduction blunts your passive. Purgatory's grounding is the one answer: zone his escape path, not his feet.

edits.before: Use Q Null Sphere shield to absorb your W burst
edits.after: Soak your on-hit magic damage with Null Sphere

edits.before: Track Kassadin’s Riftwalk: His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Commit only while it is down.
edits.after: Purgatory grounds — inside the zone Riftwalk is off. Null Sphere's shield absorbs magic only; your W's true damage passes.

edits.before: His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Only commit once it is down or baited.
edits.after: W refunds part of its self-damage and deals true damage his Null Sphere shield cannot absorb.

edits.before: Kassadin wins by landing Riftwalk, denying your pattern, and forcing the all-in before your pattern comes online.
edits.after: Kassadin wins by surviving to 6, stacking Riftwalk out of your combo, and scaling past your pre-6 pressure window.

edits.before: A poke war you enter at 125 range — pay the toll early, then one blink turns his kite into a coffin the moment the nails land.
edits.after: He is defenceless until 6 and slippery after it — take everything early, then let Purgatory's grounding be the only leash on Riftwalk.

notes: Locke's ability names are unverifiable (he is absent from Data Dragon), so I kept every existing name string untouched and wrote new prose in slot terms where possible. The grounding-versus-Riftwalk interaction is the single highest-value fact in this matchup and was absent from both layers; the mirror kassadin__locke already carries it, so the two sides now agree.
